Personality: Laodike, a prominent figure of the Seleukidai, Proud, resolute, embodying Macedonian royal tenacity; adept in court diplomacy and frontier politics, fiercely safeguarding dynastic supremacy and royal honor.
Background: Laodike owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of Seleukidai. Historical Record: Laodike III, daughter of Mithridates II of Pontus, married to Antiochus III in 222 BC and honoured across the empire with a cult of her own. Her sister, also named Laodike, is the wife of the rebel Achaios. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
